Anti-Netanyahu parties secure 67 seats with over 85 pct of Israeli votes counted Parties opposed to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured 67 seats in the 120-member parliament after 85.6 percent of votes were counted in Tuesday's election, according to updated official results. The Central Elections Committee said the results were based on the counting of most votes cast at regular polling stations. U.S. military raises cost estimate of Iran war to 47 bln USD The cost of the U.S. military campaign against Iran has risen to at least 47 billion U.S. dollars, up 3.5 billion dollars from early September, local media reported Tuesday. COP17 nears conclusion as negotiators make progress but face hurdles The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations (UN) Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) in the Armenian capital of Yerevan has entered its final stretch. The conference has adopted 14 decisions and secured more than 1.8 billion U.S. dollars in financial commitments. High-speed train collision kills at least 68 in Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks Wednesday in Spain, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of mourning. Sánchez called for increased safety measures to restore confidence in a high-speed rail system that was once a source of national pride. Netanyahu and top rival face postelection choices that could redefine Israeli politics JERUSALEM (AP) — Israelis braced for perhaps weeks of political uncertainty Wednesday after an election that has challenged Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s grip on power and raised the almost unthinkable possibility of some Jewish and Arab parties teaming up in an effort to unseat him. Final election results could come as early as Thursday evening, though no clear winner is expected to emerge. Arab-led parties made a historic showing, but it’s not clear if the other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right government would form a coalition with them to reach a majority of seats in parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain incredibly sensitive, and Israelis are already renewing a debate about the identity of the nation founded as a state for the Jewish people. On Wednesday, Netanyahu warned against a “dangerous government” that might include Arab parties, whose constituents make up 20% of Israel’s population. And even as it leads in the vote count, Netanyahu's Likud party claimed that Tuesday’s election was “stolen” by Arab parties and asked Israeli authorities to investigate. It did not provide specific evidence to support its claims. The elections committee has said that reports about irregularities were much lower than in previous elections. Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged despite elevated inflation WASHINGTON (AP) — The Federal Reserve kept its key rate unchanged Wednesday at about 3.9% despite stubbornly high inflation, as Chairman Kevin Warsh suggested its policies are already showing signs of having an impact. The Fed said “inflation remains elevated” in the statement it released after its two-day meeting, and added that holding off on a rate increase allows “the accumulation of more information” that will inform the Fed's next steps. The Fed raised its benchmark rate last month by a quarter-point for the first time in three years, defying President Donald Trump’s demands for rate cuts, in an effort to bring inflation back to its 2% target more quickly. The Fed is tasked by Congress to combat inflation, and it does so by lifting rates to slow borrowing and spending and reduce price increases. While Warsh declined to provide much insight into what the Fed may do next, most economists still expect the central bank to hike its key rate another quarter-point at its next meeting Dec. 8-9. Wall Street investors now see the odds of an increase then at nearly 85%, according to CME Fedwatch. “It's likely going to take one more (hike) from the Fed to get interest rates into restrictive territory,” where they can slow inflation, said Michael Reynolds, vice president for investment strategy at Glenmede, a wealth advisory firm. ... items.title: US business activity cools in October; strong demand fueling price pressures By Reuters
items.excerpt: Published Oct 23, 2026, 09:49 AM Updated Oct 23, 2026, 09:55 AM ... WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US business activity slowed modestly in October, though robust demand allowed companies to raise prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high in the coming months. S&P Global said on Friday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, slipped to 57.6 this month from a five-year high reading of 58.4 in September. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. Strength in manufacturing was offset by a slight pullback in the vast services sector. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing following what is expected to have been a strong performance in the July-September quarter. Economists expect the government’s advance gross domestic product report next week to show the economy growing at around a 3.0% annualized rate last quarter, mainly driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. The economy has so far not shown any signs of buckling under the weight of the oil price shock stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran, with savings, generous tax returns in the spring, tariff refunds, a strong stock market performance and corporate profits providing a cushion. Economists warned that the inflation fallout from the drawn-out Middle East conflict was likely to slow consumer spending this quarter. The survey’s measure of new orders received by businesses edged up to 58.2 this month, the highest level since March 2022, from 58.1 in September. The increase was mostly in the services sector, with S&P Global noting "rising domestic demand, boosted partly by precautionary stock building" and growth in exports. Its gauge of prices for output rose to 59.8, the highest reading since August 2022, from 58.4 in September. Businesses across manufacturing and services sectors raised prices. Delivery performance by suppliers to manufacturers deteriorated further. The survey’s measure of suppliers’ delivery times dropped to a more than four-year low of 38.1 from 40.9 in September. SUPPLY BOTTLENECKS INTENSIFYING "Cost pressures remain a key concern," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Supply chain bottlenecks have meanwhile intensified, and order book backlogs are growing, making it easier for companies to pass higher costs on to customers." Consumer and producer prices increased strongly in September, the government reported this month, raising concerns that inflation was fanning out across the economy. The Federal Reserve in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range. Economists expect the US central bank to stand pat at its meeting next week and hike borrowing costs again in December.

items.title: US midterms briefing: Trump expands hunt for voter fraud ahead of midterms as Obama hits trail - ABC News
items.excerpt: ## Here's what you need to know today - Presidents hit the trail: Republican President Donald Trump and Democratic former president Barack Obama are heading to Ohio and Georgia respectively to shore up votes as the US enters its last week before the midterms. These states are the sites of critical contests that could decide which party could control the US Senate for the remainder of Trump's term. Obama kept a low profile for most of this election cycle, but has hit the campaign trail in recent days to deliver some fiery speeches against his successor. - Hunt for non-citizen voters: The Trump administration has issued more than 100 subpoenas demanding records on tens of thousands of voters in at least 13 states, Reuters reports. It's the latest in an effort to uncover evidence of voter fraud. Election officials and lawyers worry the investigations could undermine confidence in election systems, and be used to attack the legitimacy of narrow races. Since Trump returned to office, prosecutors have accused at least 147 people of illegally voting, Reuters reports, but the cases amount to fewer than one for every million people who voted in 2024. - The tale of two Dans: If you missed it, Republican senator Dan Sullivan is defending his Alaska seat from independent candidate … Dan Sullivan. It's been a point of ire for Republicans for months, with (unsuccessful) challenges to throw the newcomer off the ballot making it all the way to the Alaska Supreme Court. They argue the second Sullivan (AKA, Dan J Sullivan) is running just to confuse voters. Dan J Sullivan has maintained he's running for legitimate reasons. But a New York Times exclusive has put a new twist in the tale, reporting that campaign aides for Democratic candidate Mary Peltola sought a spoiler candidate by the name of Dan Sullivan to undermine the senator back in 2025.

items.excerpt: Live By Aakash Kumar Updated: Thursday, October 29, 2026, 9:44 [IST] Entertainment News Live Updates Today: Thursday (October 29) has brought several new developments across Bollywood, television, and the OTT space. From major box office milestones and celebrity updates to the latest TV twists and streaming news, the entertainment industry has plenty to keep fans busy. ## ENTERTAINMENT NEWS UPDATES - OCTOBER 29, 2026 Among the key updates, Sai Pallavi's comments about Ravana have sparked social media buzz after a video from the Los Angeles premiere of Ramayana went viral. The actress spoke about the importance of understanding Indian culture and the lessons people can learn from the mythological epic. However, her statement that Ravana is 'not all bad' caught the attention of viewers, with several users sharing different opinions about her remarks. Priyanka Chopra gave fans a glimpse of her Karwa Chauth special DIY mehendi, which featured the initials of her husband, Nick Jonas, and daughter, Malti. In another news, Bigg Boss 20 will witness another physical fight between Gullu and Yung DSA. Now, it'll be interesting to see if one of them will be eliminated like Nukul Dhull or not. Here's a quick roundup of the latest entertainment news, including the biggest film, television, and OTT updates you shouldn't miss today. ## Bigg Boss 20: Will Gullu Get Eliminated Due To Physical Violence? The latest Bigg Boss 20 promo features a physical altercation between Gullu and Yung DSA, raising questions about whether Gullu could face eviction from the show. The incident has reminded viewers of Nakul Dhull's exit, which followed a similar physical fight during his stint on the reality show. With the new promo creating buzz, viewers are now wondering whether Bigg Boss will take strict action against Gullu or handle the matter differently. However, his possible elimination remains unconfirmed, and the show's decision is awaited. > Game Over For Gullu Aka Ullu 💀 #YungDSA #BiggBoss20 https://t.co/Aj5FUsUFdg > > — MC STAN ARMY 🦁🐅 (@abdisha66805687) October 28, 2026 Oct 29, 2026, 9:44 am IST ## Priyanka Chopra's Mehendi For Husband Nick Jonas On Karwa Chauth Karwa Chauth celebrations are incomplete for many married Indian women without applying mehendi. Priyanka Chopra also embraced the tradition this year, sharing a glimpse of her special DIY mehendi design with fans. On Thursday, the actress posted pictures of the mehendi she applied herself. The design featured the initials of her husband, Nick Jonas, and their daughter, Malti Marie Chopra Jonas, making it a personal tribute to her family. Sharing the pictures on Instagram, Priyanka captioned the post, "DIY..Piya ke naam ki (in the name of my husband).. happy karwachauth to all those celebrating."
